facts.statement: Macrogryphosaurus is an elasmarian dinosaur from the Upper Cretaceous of Patagonia, Argentina, meaning "big enigmatic lizard".
facts.quote: Macrogryphosaurus (meaning "big enigmatic lizard") is a genus of elasmarian dinosaur from the Coniacian-aged (Upper Cretaceous) Sierra Barrosa Formation (Neuquén Group) of Argentina in Patagonia.

facts.statement: An articulated, nearly complete skeleton was discovered in May 1999 at Mari Menuco Lake, Argentina, by the National University of Comahue.
facts.quote: In May 1999, during field work at Mari Menuco Lake, Argentina (sixty kilometres northwest of Neuquén) conducted by the National University of Comahue, an articulated, nearly complete dinosaur skeleton was discovered and excavated.

facts.statement: The fossil was found by a young boy named Rafael Moyano.
facts.quote: It was brought to the attention of the palaeontologists by young boy Rafael Moyano, who had discovered it.

facts.statement: The species was formally described and named in 2007 by Jorge O. Calvo, Juan D. Porfiri, and Fernando E. Novas.
facts.quote: The species would be described and named Macrogryphosaurus gondwanicus in 2007, in a study authored by Jorge O. Calvo, Juan D. Porfiri, and Fernando E. Novas.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen MUCPv-32 includes an essentially complete set of vertebrae, ribs, four thoracic plates, pectoral girdles, and a sternum.
facts.quote: The holotype specimen, MUCPv-32, consists of an essentially complete set of vertebra, a number of ribs, four mineralized thoracic plates, both sides of the pectoral girdle, and a sternum.

facts.statement: The dinosaur is noted for bony plates on its thorax and was identified as a large ornithopod.
facts.quote: Noted for bony plates on its thorax, it was identified as a large species of ornithopod.

facts.statement: The species is estimated to have reached around 6 meters in length, though the known specimen may not have been fully grown.
facts.quote: It has been estimated to have been around 6 m in length, though the only known individual may not have been fully grown.

facts.statement: It is the largest known species of South American ornithopod excluding Hadrosauridae and the largest known elasmarian species.
facts.quote: As such, it is the largest species of South American ornithopod outside of Hadrosauridae, and the largest species of elasmarian.

facts.statement: A remarkable feature is its series of mineralized thoracic plates, also called intercostal plates.
facts.quote: One of the most remarked upon features of the taxon is its mineralized thoracic plates, also referred to as intercostal plates.

facts.statement: Its short torso, combined with a fused birdlike sternum, would have been rather stiff.
facts.quote: Along with a fused, birdlike sternum, its short torso would have been rather stiff in nature.

facts.statement: Phylogenetic analysis links it to Talenkauen, leading Calvo and colleagues to propose the new clade Elasmaria for both genera.
facts.quote: Phylogenetic analysis indicates that it is related to Talenkauen, and Calvo and colleagues proposed a new clade, Elasmaria, for the two genera.

facts.statement: It lived during the Coniacian age, approximately 89.8 to 85.7 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Coniacian to Coniacian (89.8 to 85.7 million years ago)

facts.statement: As a basal iguanodontian, it was likely a bipedal herbivore.
facts.quote: Como otros iguanodontianos basales debió haber sido un herbívoro bípedo.

facts.statement: The holotype MUCPv-321 is estimated at 6 meters long, and likely had not reached adult size due to unfused vertebrae.
facts.quote: Macrogryphosaurus es más largo que Talenkauen, para MUCPv-321se estima un largo de 6 metros y probablemente el individuo no había alcanzado su tamaño de adulto basándose en la falta de fusión de algunas vértebras.

facts.statement: The species name gondwanicus refers to the ancient supercontinent Gondwana.
facts.quote: The specific epithet gondwanicus refers to the ancient continent of Gondwana.

facts.statement: Dr. Stephen F. Poropat described the fossil preservation as "amazing."
facts.quote: The preservation of the fossil was described by Dr. Stephen F. Poropat as "amazing" in nature.

facts.statement: A complete osteology was published in 2020 by Sebastián Rozadilla, Penélope Cruzado-Caballero, and Jorge O. Calvo.
facts.quote: M. gondwanicus received a complete osteology in 2020, a study published in Cretaceous Research by Sebastián Rozadilla, Penélope Cruzado-Caballero, Jorge O. Calvo.

facts.statement: Researchers consider the genus important because it is the largest known elasmarian and its complete remains inform on the group's anatomy.
facts.quote: They considered the genus to be of importance, due to being the largest known elasmarian species, and for the completeness of its known remains, informing on the anatomy of the group.

rejected.statement: The generic name combines Greek roots meaning "large," "enigmatic," and "lizard."
rejected.quote: The generic name was derived from the Greek macro, meaning large, grypho, meaning enigmatic, and saurus, meaning lizard.
